description: A pure CALCULATION node — carve door/window openings into a partition graph: graph in, graph out. Draws nothing on canvas.
instructions:
A value-only node: it takes a partition GRAPH and returns a graph whose edges carry `type` ("wall" | "opening"). It has no geometry input or output and draws nothing on the canvas.

INPUT: graph takes { "nodes": [{ "id", "x", "y" }, ...], "edges": [{ "from_node_id", "to_node_id", "thickness" }, ...] } — coordinates in metres, local to the anchor. Wire a Merge Graph (or BSP) val-graph into valin-graph.

WHAT IT DOES: it traces the planar faces of the graph — the largest face per component is the OUTER boundary, every other face is a ROOM. It then centres one OUTER opening (window, `Outer opening width`) on EACH boundary edge, and one INNER opening (door, `Inner opening width`) on the LONGEST interior wall of EACH room (deduped so a shared wall opens once). A carved edge A→B becomes A→P1 (wall) · P1→P2 (opening) · P2→B (wall); the jamb nodes are added and the wall parts keep the edge's thickness. Walls shorter than the opening plus a jamb each side stay solid.

OUTPUT: val-graph publishes the graph with every edge tagged `type` "wall" or "opening". Wire it into Mitered Join — with "Use same width for all" OFF it strokes the walls (at their own thickness) and SKIPS the openings, leaving real gaps.

Every parameter is wireable (valin-*).
